Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm
you're comfortable continuing?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Let's start with what happened. Can you walk me through the collision in Baytown?
A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road heading east. The car behind me didn't stop in time and hit my rear
bumper pretty hard. I felt a jolt and my head snapped back against the headrest.
Q: Were you able to drive your vehicle from the scene?
A: Yes, it was still drivable, but I pulled into a parking lot nearby because my neck and lower back were already
starting to hurt.
Q: Did you call for medical help or go to a doctor?
A: I went to an urgent care clinic the same afternoon. They looked at my back and neck, took some X-rays, and
diagnosed a back strain. They gave me muscle relaxers and told me to rest and avoid lifting.
Q: Have you had any follow-up treatment since then?
A: I've been to physical therapy twice a week. My back is still sore when I sit for long periods, and bending over to
pick things up is hard.
Q: Did you have any pain or problems with your back before this collision?
A: No, nothing serious. I had some minor stiffness now and then from sitting at a desk, but I never needed treatment
for it.
Q: Is there anything else you want to add about the accident?
A: Just that the other driver admitted at the scene that they were lokoing at their phone. I'd like that noted.
Q: Thank you. We'll follow up with the next steps by mail. Have a good day.
A: Thanks, you too.
</page>
